questions.q: What does the Filter transformation do?
options: Keeps only rows matching a boolean expression — a visual WHERE clause
Renames columns without changing row values
Creates new columns using an expression
Combines two data streams into one
questions.explain: Filter evaluates a boolean expression per row, similar to a SQL WHERE clause — only matching rows continue downstream.

questions.q: What does the Select transformation change?
options: Only the column list — renaming, dropping, or reordering columns, without touching row values
Row values, by applying an expression to each one
Which rows pass through, based on a condition
The data flow's integration runtime
questions.explain: Select reshapes the column list only — a useful cleanup step after a Join brings in duplicate-named columns, for example — but it never changes what's actually stored in a row.

questions.q: How do you overwrite an existing column's value with Derived Column, rather than creating a new one?
options: Select the existing column from the dropdown, instead of typing a new name
Derived Column can only ever create new columns, never overwrite existing ones
Delete the column first with a Select transformation
Use the Filter transformation instead
questions.explain: Typing a new name in the Column box creates a new column; selecting an existing column from the dropdown overwrites it with the new expression's result.

questions.q: What does a column pattern let you do in Derived Column?
options: Apply the same expression logic to every column matching a metadata rule, automatically
Only apply to exactly one column at a time
Delete every column that doesn't match a pattern
Column patterns only work inside the Filter transformation
questions.explain: A column pattern matches columns by metadata rules (like a name prefix) and applies the same derived logic to every match — useful for flexible or drifting schemas.

questions.q: What's a real example use of Derived Column overwriting an existing column?
options: Converting a text Rating column to an integer type using toInteger(Rating)
Deleting the Rating column entirely
Renaming Rating to CustomerRating
Filtering out rows where Rating is missing
questions.explain: Selecting the existing Rating column and setting its expression to toInteger(Rating) keeps the same column name but changes its actual type and values.
